title: Case Processing SOP for Thymus
author: Marda Jorgensen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbgmiju6
materials: Sample Archiving: a. All materials obtained for this program will be inventoried by the University of Florida Tissue Mapping Center (UF TMC) and archived in the Organ Processing and Pathology Core (OPPC) until use. b. Samples will be released for use or shipped to collaborator(s) upon request by the Principle Investigator.

steps.title: Identify tissue and assign case number
steps.instruction: Confirm the received specimen is thymus (TH) and assign a case number using the template YY‑NNN (two‑digit year, hyphen, three‑digit sequential number starting at 001).

steps.title: Assign sample nomenclature
steps.instruction: Record the sample type using the approved abbreviations: FFPE (Formalin Fixed Paraffin Embedded), Fixed OCT Block (Formalin Fixed Frozen Embedded), Fresh OCT Block (Fresh Frozen Embedded), or Fresh Tissue piece (in 4 % PFA or complete medium in a 50 mL conical).

steps.title: Label cassettes, cryomolds and containers
steps.instruction: Create labels as follows: for cassettes and cryomolds print or write legibly with a cassette printer or permanent ink; Line 1 = Case ID + sample‑type abbreviation; Line 2 = Block number (coordinate region followed by lateral‑to‑medial position in 1 cm cubes; add “FX” for fixed‑frozen tissue). Apply the same format to dishes, foil wraps or other containers.

steps.title: Record processing data and photograph organ
steps.instruction: Enter all required fields on the Case Worksheet (case ID, receipt date, shipment details, anomalies, processing start/end times, staff, tissue types, aliquot numbers, quality notes). Take photos of the intact organ from all angles, orienting the tissue horns at the top and the cardiac surface face‑down.

steps.title: Collect RNA‑QC tissue and flash freeze
steps.instruction: Using RNase‑free technique, excise a 0.5 cm³ cube from an interior, non‑coordinate region of the organ for RNA quality control and immediately flash‑freeze it in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Harvest common‑coordinate regions
steps.instruction: Cut 1 cm‑thick cross‑sectional slabs of the organ, slide each slab slightly to the right of the residual tissue, and photograph the location. Using a ruler or grid, map each slab’s position. Then:

substeps.instruction: Cut a 1 cm‑wide strip through the centre of each slab and photograph the strip’s position before removal.
Divide each strip into individual 1 cm³ blocks (use a 1 cm × 1 cm tissue matrix if helpful) and photograph each cut, preserving orientation and order.

steps.title: Fix blocks in neutral buffered formalin (NBF)
steps.instruction: Place the 1 cm³ blocks (as recorded on the Diagram Worksheet) into NBF‑labeled cassettes, add at least 20 mL of NBF per cassette, and agitate at room temperature. After 20–24 h, transfer cassettes to 70 % ethanol; process the tissue within 3 days.

steps.title: Fix blocks in 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA)
steps.instruction: Place the 1 cm³ blocks into PFA‑labeled cassettes, add at least 20 mL of 4 % PFA per cassette, and agitate at room temperature. After 20–24 h, move cassettes to 70 % ethanol; process within 3 days.

steps.title: Process blocks for frozen OCT (FX)
steps.instruction: Place the 1 cm³ blocks into FX‑labeled cassettes, immerse in at least 20 mL of 4 % PFA per cassette, agitate at room temperature for 20–24 h, then follow the SOP at https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.basniede for processing and embedding.

steps.title: Embed fresh OCT blocks
steps.instruction: Place the 1 cm³ blocks (as indicated on the Diagram Worksheet) into labeled cryomolds filled with OCT, maintaining orientation. Follow the SOP at https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcwsixee for processing, embedding, and transport of the frozen blocks on dry ice.

steps.title: Prepare blocks for CLARITY analysis
steps.instruction: Submerge each 1 cm³ block in 4 % PFA using a minimum ratio of 20 volumes fixative to tissue volume; fix for 20–24 h at room temperature with gentle agitation. Then transfer the tissue to hydrogel solution and incubate for 5 days at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare blocks for 10X analysis
steps.instruction: Place each 1 cm³ block into a 50 mL tube containing 25 mL complete DMEM/F12 medium. Store the tubes in a refrigerator (4 °C) until the tissue is released for downstream isolation.

steps.title: Follow collaboration protocol B if needed
steps.instruction: If the tissue is designated for a collaborative project, identify “protocol B” on the worksheet and execute the external lab’s specified procedures.
